title: WLF bank charter from the OCC
summary: WLF's subsidiary WLTC Holdings applied to the OCC in January 2026 for a national trust bank charter, World Liberty Trust Co., N.A., to issue and custody USD1. The OCC granted preliminary conditional approval on 14 Aug 2026 (CD #1385), and the president does appoint the OCC's head, Comptroller Jonathan Gould. As of Nov 2026 no final approval had been reported. Two details are off: there was one application, not several 'charters', and the 'career staff' line comes mainly from the OCC's own approval letter, while WLF (Zach Witkoff) issued a general denial of favoritism. The WSJ later reported, citing anonymous sources, that a Tahnoon bin Zayed-backed vehicle (StringZ) owns 49% of the bank's parent and the Trump family about 38%.

sub_claims.statement: World Liberty is applying for bank charters.
sub_claims.finding: WLTC Holdings LLC filed a single de novo national trust bank charter application with the OCC (dated 2026-01-05, announced 2026-01-07). The proposed bank would issue, redeem and custody USD1, would carry no FDIC insurance, and would not take deposits or make loans. The plural 'charters' overstates it.

The OCC granted preliminary conditional approval on 2026-08-14 (Corporate Decision #1385), about 221 days after filing. Conditions include at least $20M of tier 1 capital and liquid assets equal to the greater of $10M or 50% of that capital. The capital is due within 12 months and the bank must open within 18 months. The approval is not final and can be rescinded.

sub_claims.statement: The president appoints the head of the OCC, which regulates the bank.
sub_claims.finding: The Comptroller is nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate for a 5-year term. Trump nominated Jonathan Gould, who was confirmed 50-45 on 2025-07-10 on a party-line vote. The OCC would charter and supervise the trust bank.

The Trump family holds a large WLF stake. CD #1385 lists passivity commitments from affiliated investors, including DT Marks SC LLC and StringZ Holding RSC (DE) LLC. Audit update: the WSJ reported on 2026-08-27, citing people familiar with the matter, that StringZ is backed by a group led by Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed and holds 49% of WLTC Holdings, the bank's parent, while a Trump-family-linked entity holds about 38%. That is the largest single stake. It is single-source (WSJ with anonymous sources, relayed by The Block and Cointelegraph). The OCC documents confirm StringZ as an investor bound by passivity commitments but do not name its backer or give stake sizes. Warren had asked in Feb 2026 whether a UAE company was a principal shareholder; Gould declined to discuss the application.

sub_claims.statement: WLF denies special treatment and says the approval was conducted by career staffers.
sub_claims.finding: Zach Witkoff denied favoritism and said WLF welcomes 'continuous scrutiny from federal regulators.' The 'career OCC staff reviewed the application' language is in the OCC's decision letter, which also rejected the conflict-of-interest comments and said nonpolitical examiners would supervise the bank. No primary WLF quote crediting career staff was found.

corrections: Claimed: 'bank charters' (plural). The record shows: one OCC national trust bank charter application by WLTC Holdings LLC for World Liberty Trust Company, N.A.

Claimed: WLF said the approval was conducted by 'career staffers'. The record shows: the phrase appears in the OCC's own preliminary conditional approval letter (CD #1385), and WLF's public response was a general denial of favoritism.
The charter is a limited-purpose trust charter (no deposits, no lending, no FDIC insurance), and the approval is conditional, not final.
denials_and_context: The OCC says career staff reviewed the application under statutory criteria, rejected conflict-of-interest objections as grounds for denial, and says nonpolitical examiners will supervise the bank.
Comptroller Gould refused Sen. Warren's Jan 2026 request to pause the review until Trump divests, calling the charter process 'apolitical and nonpartisan.'
Zach Witkoff denies favoritism and says the charter ensures permanent OCC supervision that 'will outlast the Trump administration.'

Context: in Dec 2025 the OCC conditionally approved similar crypto trust charters for Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos, so WLF's approval fits a broader policy, though critics say Gould pushed charters that career staff once viewed skeptically.

Critics include Warren, NCRC, Americans for Financial Reform and House Democrats. On 2026-08-15 Warren and colleagues introduced the Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act (S. 5389) to bar such approvals and end this charter.
The characterisation 'never seen anything like this' is opinion, not a checkable fact.
The WSJ's 49% StringZ/Tahnoon report (2026-08-27) rests on anonymous sources; the OCC's public decision does not identify StringZ's backer. A White House spokeswoman denied any conflicts of interest.
